::: {.callout-important}
## Not part of UIAO
The AAN book series and this training program are **companion material for
the federal vertical — they are not part of UIAO**. The UIAO core is
vertical-agnostic ([ADR-085](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-085-universal-enterprise-positioning.md));
the AAN corpus is external federal-modernization content that UIAO's
conformance tooling happens to consume as evidence. Nothing on these pages
is UIAO canon, defines UIAO doctrine, or is scoped for a `UIAO_NNN`
allocation. These pages are hosted here for convenience alongside the
adapter that binds the books' evidence.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Living program — expansion expected
This program is a **research-driven living curriculum**. It launches with the
program charter, the two track outlines, and a first-pass vendor training
catalog. As research continues, modules gain per-book lesson pages, labs,
assessment rubrics, and additional vendor offerings. See
[Expansion roadmap](#expansion-roadmap).
:::

## What this program is

The Federal Application-Aware Networking (AAN) series is a **15-book corpus**
(Book 00 through Book 14) that documents a complete federal network
modernization: landing zone and IPAM, network and telecommunications
modernization, data-platform authentication, privileged access, vulnerability
management, data protection, detection engineering, business continuity,
supply-chain risk, program governance, and PII transparency. The books live in
draft staging at
[`inbox/Application Aware Networking/`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/inbox/Application%20Aware%20Networking)
and are bound to FedRAMP 20x evidence slots by the
[`fedramp_aan_catalog` adapter](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog).

The AAN Training Program teaches that corpus in **two tracks**:

| Track | Page | Audience | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Track A — Compliance** | [Compliance track](compliance-track.html) | ISSOs / ISSMs, assessors, ConMon operators, compliance leads | Can state, for each of the 15 books, which NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls it closes, which FedRAMP 20x KSI category evaluates that closure, and how the evidence flows through the UIAO conformance pipeline |
| **Track B — Implementation** | [Implementation track](implementation-track.html) | Network, platform, database, identity, and security engineers | Can implement the architecture each book describes and produce the machine-readable evidence Track A consumes |

A third page, the [Vendor training catalog](vendor-training-catalog.html),
maps each book to existing external training from the vendors whose products
the books deploy (Microsoft, Infoblox, Cisco, AWS, and others), plus
federal/compliance training sources (CISA, FedRAMP, NIST).

## Relationship to UIAO

- This program is **separate from**
  [UIAO_125 Training Program](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/program-training.md)
  (Contributor + Operator tracks). UIAO_125 teaches the UIAO substrate; this
  program teaches the **federal AAN book series**, which is not UIAO
  material. The only connection is mechanical: the
  `fedramp_aan_catalog` conformance adapter reads the books' artifacts as
  evidence, the same way UIAO adapters read any external vendor's output.
- Per [ADR-085](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-085-universal-enterprise-positioning.md),
  the UIAO core is vertical-agnostic. Describing this curriculum as part of
  UIAO would itself be a positioning bug under that ADR.
- The compliance backbone follows the
  [Federal AAN / ConMon Compliance Gap Roadmap](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/inbox/Application%20Aware%20Networking/federal-aan-conmon-gap-roadmap.md)
  and the slot bindings in
  [`fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings/`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Provenance status
The AAN books currently live under `inbox/` — the repo's **draft staging**
surface. They are external companion material, not UIAO canon, and are not
on a canonization path. If the books move to their own home, the links
below follow them. Treat control-closure counts as working figures from the
gap roadmap, not attested facts.
:::

## The 15-book corpus

Each book now has a **module page** — objectives, key concepts,
implementation sequence, compliance hooks, labs, pitfalls, and vendor
training pointers, all derived from the book's actual content. The module
page links to the canonical manuscript source.

| Book | Module page | Domain | Evidence slot(s) | KSI category |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | [Executive Summary](books/book-00.html) | Orientation | — | — |
| 01 | [SSA Landing Zone, IPAM & FedRAMP](books/book-01.html) | DDI / IPAM landing zone | 2 — addressing | KSI-PIY |
| 02 | [Network Modernization](books/book-02.html) | SD-WAN, SASE, UC | 3 — network | KSI-CNA |
| 03 | [Federal Telecommunications Modernization](books/book-03.html) | Entra ID, ZTNA, cloud voice | 1 — identity | KSI-IAM |
| 04 | [SQL Server Authentication Modernization](books/book-04.html) | Data-platform identity | 1 — identity | KSI-IAM |
| 05 | [SQL Server Implementation Guide](books/book-05.html) | Data-platform runbook | (procedural evidence for Book 04) | — |
| 06 | [Database Consolidation & Network Physics](books/book-06.html) | Database architecture | 3 — network | KSI-CNA |
| 07 | [Privileged Access Management](books/book-07.html) | Entra PIM + PAW | 1 — identity; 5 — endpoint | KSI-IAM, KSI-PIY |
| 08 | [Vulnerability Management](books/book-08.html) | Defender VM + KEV | 4 — telemetry; 5 — endpoint; 6 — security | KSI-MLA, KSI-PIY, KSI-CMT |
| 09 | [Data Protection (Purview)](books/book-09.html) | Purview + Key Vault CMK | 4 — telemetry | KSI-MLA |
| 10 | [SIEM / XDR Detection](books/book-10.html) | Sentinel detection engineering | 4 — telemetry; 6 — security | KSI-MLA, KSI-CMT |
| 11 | [Business Continuity](books/book-11.html) | Contingency planning | 7 — continuity | KSI-RPL |
| 12 | [Supply Chain Risk Management](books/book-12.html) | SBOM, VDR/VER, BOD 26-04 | 6 — security | KSI-CMT |
| 13 | [Program Management & Governance](books/book-13.html) | PM charter | 6 — security | KSI-CMT |
| 14 | [PII Processing & Transparency](books/book-14.html) | PT control family | 5 — endpoint | KSI-PIY |

Slot definitions, KSI categories, and NIST anchors come from the adapter's
[mapping files](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings)
— the same data the conformance pipeline evaluates, so the curriculum cannot
silently drift from the evidence model.

## Program structure

1. **Orientation (both tracks)** — read Book 00 and the
   [gap roadmap](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/inbox/Application%20Aware%20Networking/federal-aan-conmon-gap-roadmap.md);
   understand the FedRAMP 20x timeline (Class A opened August 2026; 20x
   mandatory January 2027; BOD 26-04 VDR/VER due December 7, 2026).
2. **Pick a track** — [Track A Compliance](compliance-track.html) or
   [Track B Implementation](implementation-track.html). The tracks share the
   corpus but read it differently: Track A reads books as *control-closure
   evidence*; Track B reads them as *build instructions*.
3. **Supplement with vendor training** — each module points into the
   [vendor training catalog](vendor-training-catalog.html) for the underlying
   product skills (Entra, Sentinel, Purview, Infoblox DDI, SD-WAN, …).
4. **Capstone (both tracks)** — produce or evaluate a KSI evidence bundle
   with the `uiao` CLI (`uiao ksi evaluate`, `uiao oscal ksi-ar`,
   `uiao oscal generate`) against the seven AAN evidence slots.

## Completion criteria

Borrowing the pattern of UIAO_125 §4 (no parallel certification system),
without being part of that program:

- **Track A** — a clean walk of all seven slot mappings: for each slot, name
  the books that feed it, the KSI category that evaluates it, and produce a
  `uiao oscal ksi-ar` run showing each KSI verdict (satisfied /
  not-satisfied / not-evaluated), with a short written gap statement for
  anything not yet evaluable.
- **Track B** — implement (or lab-simulate) one module end-to-end and land
  its evidence artifact where the slot mappings can bind it, verified by
  regenerating the KSI Assessment Results (`uiao oscal ksi-ar`) and seeing
  the slot's verdict reflect the new evidence.

## Expansion roadmap

Planned growth as research continues (tracked in ordinary PRs against this
directory):

- ✅ **Per-book module pages** — shipped: all 15 books have module pages
  (see the table above) with objectives, key concepts, implementation
  sequence, labs, and pitfalls derived from the manuscripts. Next
  iteration: reading checkpoints and quiz items.
- ✅ **Vendor catalog verification** — first research pass complete: the
  original research-queue vendors (Zscaler, Netskope, ServiceNow, Linux
  Foundation/OpenSSF, ISACA, IAPP, Tenable, Qualys) are now catalog rows
  with verified training-portal URLs.
- **Lab environments** — scripted tenant/lab setups for the Microsoft-stack
  modules (PIM, Sentinel, Purview) and DDI modules.
- **Assessment rubrics** — per-slot scoring sheets for Track A capstones.
- **A permanent home** — this material is not UIAO and will not be
  canonized as a `UIAO_NNN` spec; if the AAN corpus moves to its own
  repo/product, the program moves with it.
